prompt_text:
Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that sends failed messages to a dead-letter destination using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 2 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Option 3 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Option 4 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 5 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 6 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
from azure.servicebus import ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusMessage
import json

def handle_messages_with_dead_lettering(queue_name: str, message_to_test: dict):
    """
    Sends a test message to an Azure Service Bus queue, then receives and attempts to process it.
    If processing fails (simulated by message content), the message is moved to the
    dead-letter sub-queue using Azure Service Bus's dead_letter_message capability.
    """
    connection_str = os.environ.get("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING")
    if not connection_str:
        raise ValueError("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable not set.")

    # 1. Send a test message to the main queue to ensure there's something to process
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(conn_str=connection_str) as servicebus_client:
        sender = servicebus_client.get_queue_sender(queue_name=queue_name)
        test_message_data = json.dumps(message_to_test).encode('utf-8')
        message = ServiceBusMessage(test_message_data)
        sender.send_messages(message)
        print(f"Sent test message to '{queue_name}'. Content: {message_to_test}")

    # 2. Receive and process messages, handling failures by dead-lettering
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(conn_str=connection_str) as servicebus_client:
        # Get a receiver for the main queue
        # The dead-letter queue is a sub-queue automatically created and managed by Azure Service Bus
        with servicebus_client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name=queue_name) as receiver:
            print(f"Waiting for messages on '{queue_name}'...")
            # Receive up to 1 message, waiting for a maximum of 10 seconds
            received_messages = receiver.receive_messages(max_messages=1, max_wait_time=10)

            if not received_messages:
                print("No messages received.")
                return

            for received_message in received_messages:
                try:
                    message_body = json.loads(str(received_message))
                    print(f"Processing message: {message_body}")

                    # Simulate a processing failure based on message content
                    if message_body.get("simulate_failure"):
                        raise ValueError("Simulated message processing failure.")

                    # If processing is successful, complete the message
                    print(f"Successfully processed message. Completing it.")
                    receiver.complete_message(received_message)
                    print(f"Message completed.")

                except Exception as e:
                    # If processing fails, move the message to the dead-letter queue
                    print(f"Processing failed for message. Dead-lettering it. Error: {e}")
                    receiver.dead_letter_message(
                        received_message,
                        reason="MessageProcessingError",
                        error_description=str(e)
                    )
                    print(f"Message dead-lettered to '{queue_name}/$deadletterqueue'.")
